basis: Sean, 2026-10-29: "take a stab at reasonable decisions for the items that require my input". Claude reviewed every decision flagged for Sean. Anything not listed under calls was accepted as built.

verdicts.changed: Changed: a follow-up build carries it out
verdicts.needs-you: Kept for Sean: a serious concern or his own earlier call
verdicts.deferred: Deferred: waits on work Sean postponed

D540.note: One archive per release with the program, licence, notice and README, in the checksums and provenance like every other file.

D542.note: Signed like the app; a notarised release looks its ticket up online on first run, which is how macOS treats any bare program.

D545.note: The first-run words match the app's: Privacy & Security, then Allow Anyway; Terminal users get the xattr line.

D546.note: Copying one file into place is enough for now; an installer, Homebrew tap or update check can come later.

D550.note: Per person is the only rule that holds once an owner's own vault is already post-quantum before sharing; a vault-wide gate would refuse every head of a member without a key.

D558.note: Sean, 2026-11-04: drop it. Whether another member has updated isn't something the person can act on, so nothing shows it; nothing to build.

D563.note: Sean, 2026-11-04: approved tentatively; he reviews it in the live app, and any change becomes a small follow-up.

D564.note: Sean, 2026-11-04: approved tentatively; he reviews it in the live app, and any change becomes a small follow-up.

D565.note: Sean, 2026-11-04: approved tentatively; he reviews it in the live app, and any change becomes a small follow-up.

D566.note: Sean, 2026-11-04: approved tentatively; he reviews it in the live app, and any change becomes a small follow-up.

D572.note: Item edits are safe, so only membership changes pause while something is held back; edits wait on the device like offline edits.

D573.note: One calm line with nothing to click, naming the person by login, never a device or key; Sean checks the words in the app.

D574.note: The technical detail lives on Status for support, out of the person's way.

D577.note: A persona whose only vault is shared unlocks; a new device opens it after its first sync, and nothing stands in for it on disk.

D582.note: While the whole vault is open the item follows the vault's right, which is the more accurate label; it returns to the share's right when the vault closes.

D585.note: An item shared on its own isn't a vault the person keeps, so it shouldn't use up their vault limit.

D586.note: A vault the person only has single items from uses the join line, which says what they'd expect.

D588.note: A real bug on main: removing a member or withdrawing a share breaks other recipients' items. Fixed next, in slice 50.

D591.note: One extra history entry with the same fields and edit time is honest about the re-key and moves nothing in the list.

D594.note: An item that can't open yet is on its way; a line would only worry people, and it appears at the next sync.

D596.note: A manager's rotation or a member's edit should stay readable to people who hold one item of the owner's; queued as its own fix.

D604.note: The pages-locked number grows because it now counts every key, which is the truth; no words change.

D608.note: A server crash dump shouldn't hold its keys; turning core dumps off there is the apps' rule applied to the server. Queued with D605.

D52.note: A signed-in device should renew its own session with its device key, so the account password is asked only on a new device, after a remote sign-out, or after 30 days without use. Today a session lasts 8 hours with no renewal, so a device that syncs all day asks for the password again. Built by slice 32 (#25, D400–D408).

D138.note: Sean, 2026-11-04: "Include them." Crown jewels go into locked Lockdown backups by default, sealed under the backup password, with a switch to leave them out; plain exports stay as D121 says. Built by slice 47.

D210.note: Keep the silent passkey upgrade, and add a notice afterwards ("github.com added a passkey to this login") on the item and as a toast, so nothing is saved without the person ever hearing about it. Built by slice 33 (#26, D410).

D229.note: A push relay that Lockdown runs for self-hosted servers is an ongoing service with a running cost. It waits for the native mobile apps, which you deferred under D122.

D230.note: Strength words: weak under 50 bits, fair 50 to 74, strong from 75. The default 6-word passphrase (77.5 bits) then reads strong, as it is, instead of fair. Built by slice 33 (#26, D412).

D307.note: Kept on by default. This takes back the system-wide shortcut you listed as deferred in D122; it was kept because it needed no OS-level integration. Ctrl+Shift+Space matches 1Password's quick access.

D312.note: Same notice as D210 after an upgrade that follows a password you typed yourself. Built by slice 33 (#26, D410).

D328.note: A split view stays a warning for the vault, which keeps reading and syncing, but it pauses new contact look-ups, new shares and emergency-access grants through that server until the split clears. A server showing two histories is the moment it could swap someone's keys. Built by slice 33 (#26, D413).

D346.note: Built by slice 29 (#21): the line on Security in the desktop app, the web vault and the CLI.

D371.note: The link to the device is kept. The proposed "Revoke it on Devices" hint is left out: a device that is waiting usually just needs updating, and a nudge to revoke could cost someone a device they still use.

D442.note: The status lines as built; the plural forms read naturally.

D443.note: Show then Copy keeps a code off the screen until asked, matching the app.

D444.note: Bringing the window forward reveals nothing; the app still asks for its own unlock.

D455.note: Sean asked for it after his first run on the Mac.

D456.note: The words say plainly that the file opens the account with the password, and where to keep it.

D459.note: A4 suits most of the world but not a US printer. The PDF uses US Letter where the system's region uses it (US, Canada, Mexico, the Philippines and the rest of the Letter regions) and A4 elsewhere; the first-run slice carries it, since it rebuilds the kit screen.

D482.note: Everything Lockdown keeps on the device, found by the app's identifier and its own data folder; a guard refuses anything near the top of the disk or above the home folder.

D483.note: The shared identity is erased only when no other app is named in it, so a reset can't take Mailbird's or Synapse's keys with it.

D487.note: Every kind and the edge cases Sean asked for; password age isn't checked by Watchtower yet, so 'old passwords' waits on that.

D488.note: Records Sean's Q5 call: the demo opens from first run with no account, a bar on every screen, and Leave the demo.

D466.note: The master password through --master-password-stdin, LOCKDOWN_MASTER_PASSWORD or a prompt. One follow-up: lockdown init without --name still makes a passwordless install for old scripts; that should become a refusal or a prompt, so a command-line-only install is sealed too.

D473.note: The move copies everything and switches only once it's all there; a failed move leaves the vault as it was.

D475.note: What Sean asked for: comfortable is roomier by default, compact by setting, all tokens.

D502.note: A see-through element over the menu keeps it off, which is the safe side; a follow-up adds a line saying why instead of staying silent.

D510.note: What Sean asked for: init asks or refuses, never makes a passwordless vault; the words match the app's first run.

D511.note: The kit is printed once or saved 0600, the same route as password set; the master password is never shown.

D514.note: Joining from the command line (recover, account login) should seal like the desktop's join; queued as the next build.

D515.note: Needed so a command-line-only vault can still move to your own server; it reuses the app's move unchanged.

D521.note: The join's password is the master password; a script that joined with only LOCKDOWN_PASSWORD now stops and says why, which is the safe side.

D524.note: The lock screen shows the account's login, as the desktop records it; a login always exists.

D525.note: The command line can't wait on a security key or an emailed approval yet, so it refuses in words; the desktop handles those joins.

D533.note: A join that stopped after sealing goes back to sign-in instead of a dead end, and carries on as the same device; no new words.
